speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Intersection homology, duality, and the L2 comparison
summary: The dated Fuchs heading begins on P000917; the first line of P000918 finishes the discussion of Deligne’s construction. The talk explains allowable chains, Poincar\'e duality, the two-sphere nodal example, a proposed comparison with \(L^2\)-cohomology, and isolated-singularity truncation. This continues the subject indexed in 1979-484.1--4. The catalogue’s P000916 is an undated continuation of Zakharov’s Benney-equation discussion already indexed as 1979-488.1--7: hydrostatic equations, height conservation, additional conservation laws, a Hamiltonian layer formulation, a two-horizontal-dimensional extension, kinetic interpretation, and Gelfand’s collective-equation remark. It is covered here by this explicit boundary cross-reference, without creating a second occurrence or attributing it to Fuchs.

speaker: M. I. Graev
title: Admissible families of curves and local integral geometry
summary: Graev’s actual heading is on P000918. He discusses weighted curve transforms, differential forms on curves through a point, the distinction between closure and point-supported inversion when that incidence fiber is one-dimensional, and quotienting trivial exact forms. The two explicit FA references are identified separately: Gelfand--Gindikin--Shapiro, 13(2), 1979, and Gelfand--Graev, 14(4), 1980; the second does not have the same author list. The preceding Fuchs and Zakharov material is not reassigned to Graev.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Double fibrations, differential equations, and Segre structures
summary: The actual talk occupies P000919--P000921. It passes from a two-parameter family of plane curves and its dual differential equation to incidence double fibrations, homogeneous examples, separate-coordinate equivalence, and the coframe definition of Segre structures. The explicit Inventiones reference is Faran’s 1980 paper. P000922 begins the separately dated 20 October session, so its Goncharov, Fuchs and Beilinson interventions belong to record 493. The second-order-equation discussion recurs from 1976-403.1--5.

speaker: A. B. Goncharov
title: G-structures, intersection complexes, and regular holonomic systems
summary: The session begins on P000922 with Goncharov’s definition of a G-structure and a problem about geometries on the sphere. Fuchs then revisits allowable chains, and Beilinson explains intersection complexes through differential operators, minimal extension and the regular Riemann--Hilbert correspondence, continuing through P000924. These interventions are expressly headed in the manuscript although absent from the short catalogue label. P000925 begins 27 October and belongs to records 494--495.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Elementary group problems and projective structures on the line
summary: The dated heading is on P000925. The problems concern finite symmetry groups, the topology and group law of the universal cover of SL(2,R), a triple-line cocycle, and Kirillov’s classification of locally projective structures on the real line. The material ends above Gaveau’s heading on P000926. The catalogue’s preceding P000924 still belongs to the 20 October D-module discussion.

speaker: Bernard Gaveau
title: Levi-flat fillings and gauge-covariant stochastic constructions
summary: Gaveau’s heading begins near the bottom of P000926 and continues through P000928. The first topic concerns envelopes of holomorphy and disc fillings of spheres in complex dimension two; the second constructs gauge-covariant diffusion on connection spaces with a fixed heat-kernel cutoff; the final formulas concern Feynman--Kac, spectral growth and exponential moment estimates. His brief list of possible topics is not evidence that a full scattering theorem was stated. P000929--P000930 begin the dated 3 November session and are not part of this talk.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Representation theory, noncommutative birational geometry, and sheaves
summary: The actual intervention occupies P000929, headed I.M.G. and History of representation theory. Its historical list runs through characters, Haar integration, operator algebras and Lorentz-group representations; these names are contextual remarks, not newly stated theorems or a reliable exclusive priority list. The mathematical content concerns enveloping algebras, the Gelfand--Kirillov birational conjecture, a poorly specified extension beyond polynomial coefficients, and the BGG sheaf method on projective space. The subsequent Beilinson heading on P000930 starts record 496. The Gelfand--Kirillov problem is the earlier GP-1967-21, not a new 1980 problem.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: D-affinity and localization on the flag variety
summary: The Beilinson heading is on P000930, following Gelfand’s separately catalogued historical introduction on P000929. His talk continues through P000932, outside this record’s short catalogue range. It moves from affine schemes and quasi-coherent sheaves to D-affinity, induced modules, left/right operator issues and the Beilinson--Bernstein localization theorem at the trivial infinitesimal character. The uncertainty about the converse categorical criterion is resolved in his 10 November continuation, record 498.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Cayley numbers, absolute-valued algebras, and projective planes
summary: The actual intervention is the upper part of P000933, before Beilinson’s heading. Its questions concern multiplicative norms, the finite-dimensional restriction, a possible infinite-dimensional example, projective-plane coordinatization and a geometric approach to exceptional Lie theory. The notebook does not state a unit axiom. That omission changes both the finite classification and the answer to the infinite-dimensional question, and is recorded explicitly. No content from Beilinson’s following pages is assigned to this record.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: A-affinity, projective generators, localization and transfer bimodules
summary: The actual heading is in the lower part of P000933; the talk continues through P000936. It proves the categorical affinity criterion left uncertain on 3 November, formulates the compact projective generator lemma, repeats projective-space and flag-variety localization, and begins the transfer-bimodule construction. The preceding Cayley-algebra intervention on the same page is record 499. The short catalogue range stops before most of the proof and must not determine the content boundary.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Elementary analysis exercises and rapidly oscillating integrals
summary: Four numbered exercises precede Beilinson's heading: Thomae's function and its powers, a double-limit representation of the Dirichlet function, the obstruction to a single limit of continuous functions, and Fourier integrals with quadratic, quartic, and sextic decay. These are definite questions with classical solutions, not evidence of newly announced unresolved conjectures.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Inverse and direct images of D-modules
summary: The manuscript heading on the lower part of P000937 begins this talk, following I. M. Gelfand's exercises. Beilinson constructs ordinary inverse images of left modules and transfer bimodules for direct images of right modules, tests them on point inclusions and delta modules, and introduces derived integration and its de Rham interpretation. The actual continuation reaches P000939, beyond the catalogue range. P000936 belongs to the preceding meeting.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Two exercises on derived categories
summary: The upper portion of P000940, before the explicit 24 November heading, gives an exercise separating isomorphic cohomology from a chain map and an incompletely specified dual-sphere equivalence. The latter does not determine a kernel, an equivariance convention, or a precise category; its resemblance to a Radon transform is insufficient for an exact identification.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Whitehead products and the Jacobi identity
summary: A short intervention gives the boundary-of-a-product construction of the Whitehead product and its graded Jacobi identity. The target homotopy degree is one too high in the manuscript itself; this is a faithful mathematical error, not an English translation error.

speaker: V. I. Lomonosov
title: A compressed perturbation statement for commuting operators
summary: The manuscript records a trace-class difference for two operators, a compact difference for another pair, two commutation assertions, and a claimed unitary equivalence of absolutely continuous restrictions. The primes and the operators used in the spectral subspaces do not yield a valid identifiable theorem as written. A standard scattering-theoretic repair can be proved, but is explicitly separated from any attribution to Lomonosov.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Derived direct images and holonomic modules
summary: The talk starts below the Fuchs and Lomonosov interventions on P000940 and continues through P000943. It treats composition of derived direct images, Spencer and relative de Rham complexes, Gauss--Manin connections, closed embeddings, point-fibre criteria for holonomicity, finite length, and simple modules as minimal extensions of irreducible connections. Several assertions need the distinction between a closed embedding and an arbitrary locally closed embedding.

speaker: S. P. Novikov
title: Magnetic translations, Pauli ground states, and Bloch bundles
summary:
The actual heading is on P000944; the earlier pages assigned to this record by the supplied catalog are the end of Beilinson's lectures. Novikov discusses a magnetic Schr\"odinger operator with periodic curvature and potential, the flux obstruction to ordinary Bloch theory, the explicit zero modes of the two-dimensional Pauli operator, and the topology and perturbation of their bundle over the reciprocal torus. The zero-mode results were already published in September 1980; the perturbation and topological discussion matches a paper received on 2 December 1980, the day after this seminar (\citealp[Secs.~II--IV]{dubrovinnovikov1980ground}; \citealp[Lemmas~1--2, Theorem~2]{novikov1981magnetic}).

The notebook's physical line bundle and its bundle of Bloch zero modes must be distinguished: the former has degree \(N\), whereas the latter has rank \(N\) and first Chern number \(1\) in Novikov's orientation. Gelfand's concluding suggestion of a complex or parabolic regularization in the irrational-flux case is a program, not a specified spectral theorem. The final reading assignment on \(G\)-structures, \(\mathcal D\)-structures and the Spencer resolution is recorded as an assignment, not converted into an additional conjecture.

title: YEAR 1981
summary: This catalogue record is a calendar-year divider before the 9 February MacPherson talk. No independent mathematical assertion belongs to it, so it has no occurrence-index items. The actual P000949 scan begins with the date and MacPherson heading; the catalogue divider is not represented as a separate manuscript theorem or talk. Adjacent Novikov and MacPherson material is assigned to their own manuscript headings.

speaker: Robert D. MacPherson
title: Grassmannian simplices, the dilogarithm, and convexity
summary: The talk, described as joint work with I. M. Gelfand, develops positive diagonal-torus orbit closures in real Grassmannians, hypersimplex combinatorics, cross-ratios, Pontryagin-form integration, and a five-term dilogarithm identity. It then reports Atiyah's extensions to Kähler and symplectic geometry. The unrestricted harmonic-form assertion, the use of an orbit in place of an orbit closure, and the final Hamiltonian-orbit diagram each need distinct qualifications. The construction continues the 1979 occurrences 1979-486.12--15 and 1979-487.1--2.

speaker: A. G. Khovanskii
title: Newton polygons, genus, mixed volumes, and toric compactification
summary: Khovanskii explains how Newton polygons determine the genus and punctures of a nondegenerate curve, derives root counts through boundary valuations, introduces mixed area, and connects Pick's formula and Minkowski's inequality with toric intersection theory. The notes cite his 1977 and 1978 papers and Danilov's 1978 survey. P000960 starts the 23 February meeting, so it is not part of this lecture despite the catalogue endpoint.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Dixmier operators and Grinevich’s construction
summary: The opening of the manuscript dated 23 February 1981 reports Dixmier’s commuting operators of orders four and six, then Grinevich’s extension using Tyurin parameters. The catalogue places this record in 1991; the autograph date and the surrounding 1981 sequence establish a catalogue decade error. This recovered entry precedes Cherednik’s talk in manuscript order.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: Inverse scattering, elliptic zero curvature, and Yang–Baxter structures
summary: Cherednik presents three stages of soliton theory, from scalar inverse scattering through matrix zero curvature to the Yang--Baxter equation, with elliptic examples and Landau--Lifshitz dynamics. Only the upper portion of P000961 belongs here; Khovanskii begins below it. The manuscript dates this material 23 February 1981, correcting the catalogue’s 1991 date.

speaker: A. G. Khovanskii
title: Continuation: monomial charts and fans
summary: This recovered catalogue record continues Khovanskii after the Cherednik and Gelfand interventions of 23 February. The live catalogue's decade typo had excluded it from the supplied academic-year list. Character--cocharacter pairings, cones of one-parameter subgroups, a modification chart, the completeness criterion, and the fan of the projective plane precede the separate Kazarnovskii heading. The actual manuscript date is 1981, not 1991.

speaker: B. Ya. Kazarnovskii
title: Zeros of exponential sums and mixed pseudovolume
summary: Kazarnovskii extends Newton-polytope root counting to exponential sums with complex spectra, explains mixed pseudovolume through faces and complex tangent geometry, and mentions its support-function formulation. A separately dated 2 March question by I. M. Gelfand asks for the connection with the growth indicatrix; that follow-up is included with its own speaker and date, while the neighbouring Gaussian-tail exercise is assigned to record 514.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: A diagram relating Yang–Baxter structures
summary: A short diagrammatic reprise links factorized scattering, two-dimensional statistical mechanics, quantum one-dimensional systems, and integrable equations. Belavin adds unitarity. Gelfand’s preceding Gaussian-tail exercise is retained here as an explicitly attributed intervention; his adjacent Kazarnovskii question is indexed with record 513. The detailed three-stage account is in recovered record 510, not this March entry.

speaker: A. A. Belavin
title: Inversion, crossing, and Baxter invariant curves
summary: Belavin studies matrix inversion and partial transposition, then the invariant quantities of the symmetric eight-vertex matrix. Elliptic curves appear after projectivizing and imposing generic smoothness. The notebook’s symmetry sign and the distinction between generic and exceptional orbits require qualification.

speaker: I. V. Cherednik
title: Factorized scattering and commuting transfer operators
summary: The continuation derives the Yang--Baxter relation from three-particle reordering, rewrites it in tensor notation, gives an elliptic Pauli-matrix solution, and states the commuting-transfer-operator mechanism. The index in the component relation and the tensor leg traced in the last theorem are faithfully recorded mathematical errors, not transcription mistakes.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Moser’s isospectral formulation of ellipsoid geodesics
summary: Gelfand discusses Moser’s contribution to the Chern Symposium, giving the constrained geodesic equation and a projected matrix with constant spectrum. Jacobi’s earlier integration is mentioned; the displayed matrix construction is the modern Moser formulation.

speaker: P. G. Grinevich
title: Rational commuting differential operators of rank two
summary: Grinevich explains the elliptic rank-two Krichever--Novikov construction in Tyurin parameters and its rational specializations. The Dixmier case is a choice of rational parameter, not a consequence of setting the centre parameter to zero alone.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: A Dixmier formula and algebraic curves in the Weyl division ring
summary: Kirillov gives a formal pseudodifferential description, followed by the question of rational commuting operators with a prescribed genus-two spectral curve. Gelfand proposes an embedding of the function field of any algebraic curve in the rank-one Weyl division ring. The sixth-order formula needs emendation, and the universal curve assertion remains distinct from results for generic genus-two curves or some curves of every genus.

speaker: J.-L. Brylinski
title: Verma modules and geometric realization
summary: The uncertain handwritten surname is resolved by the explicit Kashiwara collaboration and the subject. The short record defines Verma modules and gestures toward realizations on the flag variety, with an SL(2) example. It does not state a new proof of the Kazhdan--Lusztig formula.

speaker: E. Viehweg
title: Classification of threefolds after Esnault’s Bourbaki report
summary: The talk explicitly follows Hélène Esnault’s February 1981 Bourbaki exposition. Kodaira dimension, irregularity, abelian varieties, and Albanese fibrations of threefolds are summarized. A question mark in the irregularity-zero case is preserved as an incomplete classification entry, not promoted to a newly formulated conjecture.

speaker: C. Kassel
title: K-theory of spaces and arithmetic K-groups
summary: The manuscript has separate headings for Christian Kassel and Christophe Soulé, although the catalogue supplies only the Kassel record. Kassel reports Waldhausen’s programme and homotopy-ring constructions. Soulé’s contribution concerns orders of K-groups of the integers and zeta values; its bibliographic shorthand is not an exact identification of an Inventiones paper dated February 1980.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: The collisionless Vlasov description
summary: A brief introduction explains a self-consistent field generated by many charged particles whose binary collisions are neglected. The record states a modelling principle, not a quantified mean-field limit theorem.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Weinstein’s Hamiltonian formulations of continua
summary: Arnold begins with the geodesic interpretation of incompressible Euler flow, then describes reduction to coadjoint orbits and the extension to Vlasov and gauge-coupled kinetic equations. The density variable required for compressible fluid mechanics is mentioned but no full bracket is written.

speaker: A. V. Bobylev
title: Maxwell molecules and Fourier methods for Boltzmann’s equation
summary: Bobylev presents the spatially homogeneous collision equation and singles out inverse-fourth-power potentials. Fourier methods, Gaussian convolution, linearization, and the isotropic nonlinear hierarchy appear, together with remarks on exact solutions and hydrodynamic limits. Angular cutoff, function-space, and normalization assumptions must be supplied when interpreting the compact-operator claim.

speaker: B. V. Lidskii
title: Spectra of sums of Hermitian matrices
summary: Lidskii announces the recursive Horn inequalities and a connection with tensor-product multiplicities. His two-page announcement appeared in 1982, but the later literature distinguishes it from a published proof. Klyachko’s work and the Knutson--Tao saturation theorem provide the established resolution.

speaker: S. G. Krein
title: Compressible fluids, shocks, and dispersive step evolution
summary: Krein reports the diffeomorphism-group approach to compressible flow and the incompressible limit. Scalar characteristics and shock formation prompt interventions by Gelfand and Zakharov. Gelfand’s final question concerns step-like data for a polynomial regularization of Burgers’ equation; the polynomial is not specified, so distinct dispersive and dissipative cases must be separated.

speaker: G. I. Olshanskii
title: Invariant cones, Lie semigroups, and highest-weight representations
summary: Olshanskii develops semigroups of contractions, invariant cones in Hermitian Lie algebras, and holomorphic extension of unitary highest-weight representations. The primary paper was received in December 1980 and published in 1981. Properness of cones, a choice of sign, and the analytic representation category are essential qualifications absent from the shorthand notes.
